articles.title: Pope Leo XIV could star in a historic moment with the White Sox in the MLB playoffs
articles.standfirst: The pontiff is one of the Chicago team's most famous fans and has an open invitation from the franchise. His name resurfaced amid the excitement over the MLB postseason.
articles.summary: The pontiff is one of the Chicago team's most famous fans and has an open invitation from the franchise. His name resurfaced amid the excitement over the MLB postseason.
articles.body:
The Chicago White Sox are experiencing a postseason that just a few months ago seemed hard to imagine. And while the team tries to extend its surprising October run, an unexpected name is once again appearing around the franchise: Pope Leo XIV.

The pontiff is a well-known White Sox fan and has had since 2025 an open invitation to throw out a first pitch at Rate Field. For now, there is no confirmation that he will do so, but the possibility has once again gained momentum with the team now in the playoffs.

An invitation that was born after his election as Pope

The proposal emerged shortly after Robert Francis Prevost was elected pontiff in May 2025. Brooks Boyer, then head of revenue and marketing for the White Sox, stated that Leo XIV had an open invitation to return to the stadium , sit in the seat where he had watched the 2005 World Series, and throw out the first pitch at a game. He even joked about the possibility of letting him bat.

More than a year later, that invitation has a very different context. The White Sox returned to the playoffs for the first time since 2021 after going through two especially difficult seasons : they lost 121 games in 2024, a modern-era record, and another 102 in 2025. In September they clinched their playoff berth after defeating the Kansas City Royals 9-1.

"And Leo XIV has not hidden his enthusiasm. When asked whether he had had any divine influence on the qualification, he replied with a smile: “No comment. Wonderful things happen in Chicago.”

A White Sox fan long before arriving at the Vatican

The relationship between Leo XIV and the team did not begin when he was elected Pope. Robert Prevost grew up in the Chicago area and was a White Sox fan long before arriving at the Vatican. In 2005, he attended the first game of the World Series against the Houston Astros, a game that Chicago won 5-3 before completing the sweep to claim the title.

His presence was captured by television cameras. Father Bob, as he was then, was in Section 140, Row 19, Seat 2, a spot that the White Sox ultimately turned into part of the stadium’s history. The team placed a plaque and a graphic installation to commemorate that the future Pope had been seated there during that game.

The bond grew even stronger this year. In June, former catcher A.J. Pierzynski visited the Pope at the Vatican and presented him with the ball from the final out of Game 1 of that 2005 World Series. Leo XIV also received a jersey signed by Paul Konerko and, in August, the White Sox sent him one of the distinctive mitre-shaped hats they handed out to their fans.

The connection extended into the current postseason. Before the start of the Wild Card Series, a letter sent by Leo XIV from the Vatican reached Jerry Reinsdorf, chairman of the White Sox. In it, he expressed gratitude for the organization's gestures and highlighted the role of sports in creating bonds of friendship and solidarity.

Now there remains a scene that still belongs to the realm of possibility: Leo XIV on the mound at Rate Field, with a ball in his hand and before thousands of White Sox fans. The invitation already exists. The team is in October. And the Pope, for now, has not closed that door either.

articles.title: Lance Broadway cause of death: Former MLB pitcher and Marvel actor found dead at 43
articles.standfirst: Broadway appeared in Olympus Has Fallen and Marvel's Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D
articles.summary: Broadway appeared in Olympus Has Fallen and Marvel's Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D
articles.body:
Lance Broadway , the former Major League Baseball pitcher who went on to appear in Hollywood productions including Olympus Has Fallen and Marvel's Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D., has died at the age of 43 under unexplained circumstances.

The former Chicago White Sox and New York Mets player was discovered inside a stairwell at an apartment complex in Dallas, Texas, on Tuesday, November 17, according to information from local authorities.

Police reportedly responded to a 911 call at approximately 6:40 p.m. after someone discovered Broadway 's body. His death was subsequently confirmed through the Dallas County Medical Examiner's Office.

However, officials are yet to establish a cause of death, with further medical testing required before investigators can determine what happened.

The news has brought renewed attention to Broadway 's remarkable career, which saw him establish himself as a highly regarded baseball prospect before pursuing an entirely different profession in the entertainment industry.

What was Lance Broadway's cause of death?

Broadway 's cause of death remains unknown, and authorities haven't publicly disclosed any findings explaining the circumstances surrounding his passing.

The 43-year-old was found inside the Dallas apartment building on November 17, but the medical examiner's investigation is yet to produce a definitive conclusion.

Before becoming an actor, Broadway had enjoyed an impressive rise through college baseball, beginning at Dallas Baptist University before transferring to Texas Christian University .

His outstanding performances in 2005 included 15 victories, helping establish him among the country's leading pitching prospects ahead of that year's MLB Draft.

The White Sox selected him with the 15th overall pick, and he made his major league debut against the Minnesota Twins in September 2007.

Broadway remained with Chicago until 2009, when he was traded to the Mets in a deal involving catcher Ramon Castro .

After a brief stint in New York, he joined the Toronto Blue Jays organization, although he didn't make another major league appearance before moving away from professional baseball.

New career alongside Hollywood stars

Broadway 's decision to pursue acting came after he discovered an unexpected interest in improvisational performance following his baseball career.

"I don't know why but I just wanted to go take an improv class," Broadway explained during a 2013 interview. "I loved it and stuck with it."

His most prominent movie appearance came in the 2013 action thriller Olympus Has Fallen , where he portrayed Secret Service Agent O'Neil alongside Gerard Butler, Morgan Freeman and Aaron Eckhart .

Broadway compared joining an established Hollywood production to entering a major league clubhouse, explaining that both experiences required humility and a willingness to learn.

"I learned so much from these actors and everyone was so nice, but I was just watching them go about their business," he recalled.

His acting career subsequently included appearances in Lucifer, Colony, Real Husbands of Hollywood and a 2016 episode of Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D .

Broadwa y's final Instagram post, published November 7, celebrated his niece's participation in a soccer match.

"Some girls come to play soccer. My niece came to make a statement," he wrote.

His death brings a premature end to a career spanning professional sports and entertainment, while the precise circumstances surrounding his passing remain under investigation.
